chunks: Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام was asked about a man who says to his son or daughter, “May my father and mother, or my parents, be for you.” Do you see any harm in that?
He said: “If his parents are alive, then I regard that as disobedience toward them; and if they have died, then there is no harm.”

key_terms.بِأَبِي أَنْتَ وَأُمِّي: an expression meaning ‘may my father and mother be for you’ or ‘be ransomed for you’
key_terms.عُقُوقًا: disobedience or undutiful conduct toward one’s parents
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to say to one’s child, ‘May my father and mother be sacrificed for you’?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a ruling on a common expression of affection or praise directed toward one’s child. Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام teaches that saying such words while one’s own parents are still alive is a form of disrespect toward them, whereas after their death there is no problem in it.
